clue.text: One who has got round clock may be this

definitions.text: One who has got round clock may be this

parts.words: One who has got round clock may be this
parts.note: clock is slang for the face, so someone whose face is round and full like a lunar disc fits the description

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' looks like a timepiece, but it is old slang for a person's face.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a round, full face is described by an adjective likening it to the full Moon.

clue.text: Mum left with girl and quiet boy not suited to the task

parts.note: ma is mum
Ada is a girl's name
p, piano, is the musical marking for quiet
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A mother leaves with her daughter and a quiet son, none of them fit for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something badly adapted fails to fit its purpose or surroundings.

clue.text: Low-rated rower hangs around haunt

indicators.note: the rower word hangs round the outside of the haunt word

parts.note: an oar is a rower in a crew
a nest is a haunt or hideout

explanation.surface: A poorly reviewed oarsman loiters about his favourite spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hangs around' puts OAR around NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-star rating is the lowest grade in a review.

clue.text: Barrier needed when marshy land adjoins church

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A barrier is needed where boggy land borders a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a boundary barrier of posts and rails.

clue.text: Conduct brings criticism when wine's been drunk

indicators.note: the criticism word takes in, drinks, the wine word

parts.note: a comment can be a critical remark
port is a fortified wine; the 's is is

explanation.surface: Someone's behaviour is criticised after the wine has been drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'been drunk' puts PORT inside COMMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Comportment is how one carries oneself, one's behaviour.

clue.text: Put on European river

definitions.meaning: to ... clothes is to put them on
the ... flows through Russia (also Scotland and Yorkshire)

explanation.definitionFit: Putting on a garment is donning it, and the Don is a major river in Russia.

clue.text: Garments to hang down the wrong way

indicators.note: the word for drooping is read in the wrong direction, right to left

parts.note: to hang down or droop is to sag

explanation.surface: Clothes that hang badly, drooping the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns SAG into GAS, which follows TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman robes are loose outer garments worn draped over the body.

clue.text: Rickety gate at entrance to forest — eat alfresco here

indicators.note: the shaken letters stand at the entrance, before the forest
something rickety is shaky, so the letters of gate are shaken up

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire and Shakespeare's As You Like It

explanation.surface: A shaky gate at the way into a forest where you might picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rickety' turns GATE into TEAG, placed 'at entrance to' ARDEN, the Shakespearean forest.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoor garden serving tea is a place for eating in the open air.

clue.text: Mingler can turn out to be a mischievous type

indicators.note: the letters of the word can turn into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A party mingler may turn out to be a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can turn out to be' signals rearranging MINGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults.

clue.text: Southern part of Richmond-upon-Thames becomes distorted

parts.note: Kew, home of the botanic gardens, is a district of the London borough of Richmond upon Thames

explanation.surface: The south of a London borough becomes twisted out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' is the link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is slanted or out of true.

clue.text: Prolonged rest is right — extending over lunchtime!

indicators.note: the legal-right word stretches across, so it wraps round the time figure

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid
lunch is often at one o'clock, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A long rest is fine, even if it runs on past lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lunchtime' is one o'clock, giving I; 'extending over' puts it inside LIEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A morning spent staying in bed late is a prolonged rest.

clue.text: Fellow seen on the move carrying silver about — or some other metallic element

indicators.note: the man-and-shuffled letters hold something within them

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the letters of the word seen are moving about, so they are rearranged
the silver symbol is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A man spotted travelling with silver, or some other metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AG into GA, and 'carrying' places it inside MAN + NESE (the anagram of SEEN, from 'on the move').
explanation.definitionFit: Manganese is element 25, a hard grey transition metal, so it is a metallic element other than silver.

clue.text: Old school party — the lad will come later

parts.note: a do is a party
a lad is a boy
shall and will are both future auxiliaries

explanation.surface: A party at an old school, where a lad is due to arrive later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will come later' just says the SHALL piece comes last. The school is the brutal Yorkshire academy in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens invented this Yorkshire boarding establishment, run by Wackford Squeers, in Nicholas Nickleby, so it is a fictional old school.

clue.text: One may offer some illumination if somebody's lost

definitions.text: One may offer some illumination if somebody's lost

parts.words: One may offer some illumination if somebody's lost
parts.note: read as help explaining things to a confused person, but literally a powerful beam lighting up the ground when hunting for a missing person

explanation.definitionFit: A powerful beam lamp is used by rescuers looking for a missing person at night.

clue.text: Port that's gone off could make two go green

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled, so the letters of the phrase are disordered

explanation.surface: Port wine that's spoiled might turn people green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' signals rearranging TWO GO GREEN; 'could make' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital and chief port of Guyana, and the name of other port towns.

clue.text: Gem that's awful put back in container

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the container word

parts.note: a pot is a container

indicators.note: the word for awful is put back, reading in reverse

parts.note: dire means awful

explanation.surface: A gem that's horrible gets put back in its box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIRE into ERID, which goes 'in' POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a gem-quality olivine.

clue.text: Mark to go to the grave, carping audibly

indicators.note: the phrase is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: to go to the grave, carping
parts.note: to die a critic is to go to one's grave still finding fault

explanation.surface: To die still complaining, as the grumbler does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' says 'die a critic' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent or cedilla added to a letter is a mark changing its pronunciation.

clue.text: Man, dreadfully neat on the outside, quite slow

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit outside, wrapping round the name
the word neat is dreadfully mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: Dan is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man, awfully tidy outwardly, who is rather slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' turns NEAT into ANTE, and 'on the outside' puts it round DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical tempo marking meaning at a moderate walking pace, fairly slow.

clue.text: With this person around, couples cuddle

indicators.note: the self-reference word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself is me
a brace is a couple, a pair

explanation.surface: Couples cuddle when I am around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this person' is the setter, ME, turned 'around' to EM before BRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug someone is to cuddle them in your arms.

clue.text: Bird creating thrill hovering over a road

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: a buzz is a thrill

explanation.surface: A bird gives a thrill as it hovers over a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hovering over' puts BUZZ above A RD in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzard is a broad-winged hawk, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Have discussions when one has got stuck in tree

indicators.note: the numeral gets stuck inside the discussion word

parts.note: to confer is to have discussions
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: People talking things over while someone is stuck up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has got stuck in' places I inside CONFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pines, firs and spruces are cone-bearing trees.

clue.text: Stop being heard in a foreign language

indicators.note: the stopping word is heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: to finish is to stop

explanation.surface: Stop listening to a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being heard' says FINISH sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The national tongue of Finland is a foreign language to English speakers.

clue.text: One rector bursting with zeal, not putting up with anything wicked?

definitions.text: not putting up with anything wicked?

indicators.note: the rector bursting apart means his letters fly into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman full of zeal who won't put up with anything wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' signals an anagram of ONE RECTOR together with ZEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of strictly punishing every offence, however minor, means not tolerating any wrongdoing at all.

clue.text: Inspection of engineers, 200 beginning to enlist

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
CC is 200 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: only the first letter of enlist is wanted

explanation.surface: Army engineers inspect 200 recruits at the start of enlistment.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance, a military survey of ground, is an inspection.

clue.text: Wide boy has upset important people

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: A flashy dodgy dealer has upset the bigwigs.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'wide boy' is British slang for a flashy petty crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a smartly dressed small-time black-market dealer.

clue.text: How to make night toy

parts.note: the answer read as instructions says to play with the letters of a short word, which turns night into a thing-shaped rearrangement

explanation.surface: Asking how to turn day into night, with a toy.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, PLAY (an anagram signal) applied to THING, and you get NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something a child plays with is a toy.

clue.text: Is primarily misguided form of belief?

indicators.note: only the first letter of misguided is wanted

explanation.surface: Is a creed misguided at heart?
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or ideology is a system of belief, often disparaging.

clue.text: Cockney mate wants nothing for a fabric

indicators.note: nothing goes in place of the letter a

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A Cockney friend needs nothing in exchange for some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, London East End speech, gives 'china (plate)' for mate; swap its A for O (nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton cloth used for casual trousers.

clue.text: Sort of language that makes some love Dickens

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A kind of language that makes some people love Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: Vedic Sanskrit is the ancient language of the Hindu scriptures.

clue.text: Protective female could make her men hot

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase could be rearranged to make something else

explanation.surface: A woman who could get her men hot under the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' signals rearranging HER MEN HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fussy, protective woman is likened to a broody bird guarding her chicks.
